overview: Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa, at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. Most of its people live in its capital, Djibouti City. Djibouti became independent from France in 1977. Its port is vital for shipping and for trade with landlocked Ethiopia, and several countries have military bases there.

geography.text: Djibouti is mostly hot, dry desert and volcanic plateau. Lake Assal, a salt lake, is the lowest point in Africa, more than 150 metres below sea level. The country lies where three tectonic plates are pulling apart, so the land is slowly being split open.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Extremely hot and dry, one of the hottest places on Earth.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Whale sharks gather in the Gulf of Tadjoura.

history.text: The coast was home to Afar and Somali peoples and was part of trade routes across the Red Sea. France took control in the 1880s, and the port of Djibouti grew after a railway to Ethiopia was built. The territory became independent in 1977. Its position at the entrance to the Red Sea makes it home to several foreign military bases.

events.title: French foothold
events.text: France buys the port of Obock.

events.title: Railway to Addis Ababa
events.text: The railway to Ethiopia is completed.

events.title: Chinese base
events.text: China opens its first overseas military base here.

government.text: Djibouti is a presidential republic. Ismaïl Omar Guelleh has been President since 1999. Its location at the entrance to the Red Sea makes it home to military bases of the US, France, China, Japan and others.

economy.text: Djibouti's port and the railway to Addis Ababa handle most of Ethiopia's trade, making it a key gateway. Rent from foreign military bases is also a big income.

culture.text: Most people are Somali or Afar, and French and Arabic are official languages. Lake Assal, at about 155 metres below sea level, is the lowest point in Africa and saltier than the Dead Sea.

items.title: Lac Abbé
items.text: Steaming limestone chimneys in the desert.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Afar and Somali poetry and song.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Tea and coffee are shared with guests.

sport.text: Football and athletics are popular. Ahmed Salah won the bronze in the marathon at the 1988 Olympics, Djibouti's only Olympic medal.

items.text: Ahmed Salah won Olympic marathon bronze.

didYouKnow: Lake Assal in Djibouti is the lowest point in Africa, about 155 metres below sea level.
Several countries, including the US, France and China, have military bases in Djibouti.
